candidates.acceptance: attached-preamp run measures both signs, preserves sign, and reaches at least 0.5 mV output difference
candidates.name: lower_waste_sense_node
candidates.physical_move: keep about the same useful sample-to-sense coupling but remove non-signal capacitance from sense_p and sense_n
candidates.target: average sense-node capacitance <= 2.004 fF with useful coupling near 0.800 fF
candidates.why: the sampled charge would be divided over less total capacitance, so the same charge makes a larger voltage

candidates.acceptance: frontend-only transfer reaches the required ratio, then attached-preamp output reaches margin
candidates.name: stronger_useful_coupling
candidates.physical_move: increase intentional sample_p-to-sense_p and sample_n-to-sense_n coupling without growing every other sense-node capacitance at the same rate
candidates.target: useful sample-to-sense coupling >= 1.314 fF while average sense-node capacitance stays near 3.293 fF
candidates.why: more of the sampled voltage reaches the preamp input before the preamp tries to amplify it

candidates.acceptance: measured attached sense loss is reduced from about 10.47x to 2x or better, then preamp margin is retested
candidates.name: low_input_capacitance_isolation
candidates.physical_move: insert an isolation device or prebuffer whose input capacitance is materially smaller than the direct preamp gate load
candidates.target: attached sense voltage should be within 2x of the standalone measured-source voltage before gain is judged
candidates.why: the preamp should read the frontend without draining most of the frontend voltage into its input capacitance

claim_boundary.allowed: defines buildable frontend-to-preamp interface candidates and the exact measurement gate each one must pass
claim_boundary.not_allowed: does not edit layout, run a new redesigned circuit, prove latch resolution, prove SAR conversion, or write accepted converter evidence
